title: Prefetch Bloom Microcache and Slab Compactor for Tenant-aware KV Reduction
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Problem statement:

We see persistent high GPU memory pressure caused by many short-lived, low-reuse prompt fragments resident in per-GPU slab allocators. These fragments reduce available slots for high-value shared prefixes and increase evictions that harm tail latency and cost. Current heuristics rely on global fingerprints and LRU-like eviction, which are noisy for multi-tenant bursts and do not prioritize reusability across fast interleaved requests.

Goal:
Implement a lightweight CPU-side microcache that uses compact counting/bloom sketches to estimate recent fragment reuse and drive two coordinated behaviors: (1) conservative prefetching and placement decisions that avoid pinning low-value fragments onto GPU slabs, and (2) an async slab compactor that coalesces fragmented slots based on reuse signals to free contiguous GPU memory for larger context slots. The feature should reduce resident fragment count, reduce unnecessary evictions, and improve median and p95 latency under mixed tenant workloads while preserving correctness and isolation guarantees.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end can be enabled via runtime flag `--microcache=enabled` and opt in by tenant.
2) Microcache uses ~<50MB of host memory per node and introduces <1% CPU overhead on p95 load.
3) Measured reduction in GPU-resident fragment count >=25% on benchmarked mixed-tenant workload (synthetic traces + production sampling).
4) Median token latency unchanged or improved; p95 token latency improves by >=10% under the target workload.
5) No regression in correctness: model outputs must match baseline within deterministic eval set across 99.9% of samples.
6) Rollout plan and canary that supports instant rollback and monitoring dashboards for fragment counts, compact events, and eviction rates.
7) Unit and integration tests covering sketch insert/evict/hit behavior, slab compaction safety checks, and JVMMemory/allocator invariants.
8) Documentation added to /docs/runtime/cache/microcache.md and a short runbook for incidents.
implementation_notes:
Core pieces:
- Microcache sketch: use a 4-way counting-bloom sketch with 16-bit counters folded to 8-bit to bound memory. Keys are 64-bit prefix fingerprints (SipHash-based) combined with tenant-id salt.
- Hotness score: decay-based counter (exponential decay with tau=30s) computed on CPU; thresholds drive placement decisions.
- Prefetch policy: on continuous batching boundary, consult microcache to decide whether to issue a GPU prefetch/attach. Default behavior: only prefetch fragments with score >=2 and size>256 tokens.
- Slab compactor: background job running at low priority that scans slab free lists and adjacent low-hotness fragments, migrates high-hotness fragments to new contiguous slots, frees fragmented ranges, and updates resident pointers atomically. Compaction uses pause-aware incremental copying to avoid stalling inference.
- Consistency: maintain per-fragment generation/version token to avoid using stale KV pointers during compaction. Compaction creates forwarding records that are resolved by runtime when a pointer mismatch is observed.
- Telemetry: counters for sketch_hits, sketch_inserts, prefetch_decisions, compaction_runs, migrated_fragments, freed_slots, and compaction_time_ms.
- Safety: compaction disabled for tenants with strict residency pinning; admin flag to force-stop.

Implementation plan:
Phase 1: CPU-side sketch library + unit tests. Local simulation harness that replays request traces and computes hit/miss rates.
Phase 2: Integrate placement decision path (no compaction), add telemetry, run benchmarks.
Phase 3: Slab compactor implementation, safe migration path, and canary rollout on dedicated cluster.
Phase 4: Production rollout and iterative tuning of thresholds and decay constants.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Compaction may cause transient pointer redirects leading to rare incorrect KV reads. Mitigation: generation/version tokens + immediate fallback path that re-fetches based on key fingerprint.

Risk: Sketch false positives cause unnecessary prefetching. Mitigation: conservative thresholding, use counting sketch to prefer stable hot fragments, and monitor prefetch_accept_rate metric; rollback via feature flag.
Risk: Multi-tenant fairness — aggressive compaction may favor noisy tenants. Mitigation: tenant-weighted hotness metric and per-tenant max-residency limits.
Risk: Compaction CPU spikes during global burst. Mitigation: rate limit compaction jobs, backpressure and pause when node CPU exceeds threshold.
test_plan: Unit tests for sketch insert/remove/decay and collision stress tests
Integration test: enable microcache + prefetch on dedicated test cluster, replay 72h production trace, collect metrics
Chaos test: run compaction during forced GC and OOM conditions in testenv
A/B test: Canary 5% tenants vs control for 2 weeks and compare GPU memory pressure and latency
notes:
Related work: differs from prior prefix-dedup efforts by keeping the hotness estimator off-GPU and making migration decisions conservative; compaction focuses on contiguous slot recovery rather than aggressive eviction. This should interoperate with existing prefix fingerprinting ledger and the cross-tenant shard advisor.

Next steps:
- Tune sketch parameters (width/depth) after 1 week of canary data.
- Finalize PRs and documentation.
- Coordinate with Console team to add dashboards before wider rollout.
